clue.text: Two males going back to find rodent

indicators.note: going back tells the solver to read the two male animals' names from right to left as one run

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A naturalist tracks a pair of male animals back to their burrow and finds a rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns the whole run TOMRAM end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmot is a large burrowing ground squirrel, so it is a kind of rodent.

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone called Grace is having difficulties with the service in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grace' looks like a woman's name but is a verb here: to grace something is to decorate it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to beautify or decorate something.

parts.note: read slyly, a 'belief' (an ism) built on a 'system' (a method), the name of a Protestant denomination

explanation.surface: A question about the structure of Christian doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the wordplay hidden in the definition: a system is a method, and a belief is an ism.
explanation.definitionFit: Methodism is the Protestant movement founded by John Wesley, so it is a Christian creed.

parts.note: 'the' is the definite article
an MA (Master of Arts) is an academic graduate

explanation.surface: A grammar note about a female scholar who has quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb (departed) but gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a female.

parts.note: a time given over to asking questions is a television contest built around them; Question Time is also a BBC debate programme

explanation.surface: It looks like a reference to Question Time, a BBC political debate programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiz show is a broadcast programme of questions, so it is literally a time for questions.

parts.note: Victoria was a queen, and a sponge is a pudding, so a queen among puddings

explanation.surface: It looks like the name of the Victoria sponge, a classic British jam-filled cake.
explanation.walkthrough: A Victoria sponge is a British cake; here 'Victoria' is the monarch and 'sponge' stands for pudding generally. Queen of puddings is a British baked dessert of breadcrumbs, jam and meringue.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria, as a monarch who is also a sponge, is wittily a royal among desserts.

definitions.meaning: the return earned on money lent or invested

explanation.definitionFit: Money paid on a loan is a profit to the lender, and taking an interest in something is giving it your attention.

clue.text: Thus Latin's admitted to being an uncomplaining sort

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the word 'to' goes inside the Latin word

parts.note: sic is the Latin for thus

explanation.surface: A scholar notes that Latin has let in a word, producing a patient person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' puts TO inside SIC, Latin for 'thus' (as in the editorial 'sic').
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic philosopher taught endurance without complaint, so the word now means a person who bears hardship calmly.

parts.note: on can mean touching or resting upon
an impulse is a brief electrical pulse, as in a nerve

explanation.surface: A careless touch to a live wire sends a jolt through you before you know it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on a sudden urge means acting rashly, with no reflection beforehand.

clue.text: Meant well in respect of choice?

definitions.meaning: said of something done with good intentions

explanation.surface: Someone justifies a selection by saying their intentions were good.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done with good intent is done hoping it turns out well; read literally, the phrase concerns the top pick.

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals, so the verse letters go inside
short means the poem's word loses its final letter

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A poet writes a verse that is a short poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' clips ODE to OD; 'penning' then puts VI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman writer of the Metamorphoses, so he is a classical versifier.

parts.note: un is French for a
common means general or widely shared

explanation.surface: A French military general turns out to be a remarkable man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like an army officer but is an adjective meaning widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare or out of the ordinary is worth remarking on.

clue.text: Soldiers about to get pie cooked according to instructions

parts.note: the RE (Royal Engineers) are a corps of British soldiers
c (circa) means about

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of the pie are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Troops get round to making a pie by following a set of directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A cookery recipe is a set of directions for preparing a dish.

indicators.note: obtained from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fine wine sourced from the very best of Madeira.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: A trio lies about winning game

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Three cheats tell fibs to win a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the nine letters of A TRIO LIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire is a card or peg pastime played alone, where the goal is to clear the layout and so come out on top.

parts.note: fast can mean racy or morally loose
talk is spoken language

explanation.surface: Someone tries to win people over with risqué words.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk someone into something with glib, rapid patter is to win them over.

definitions.meaning: to examine something by breaking it into its components
to dismantle, working the pieces loose from one another

explanation.definitionFit: Dismantling a machine or an argument separates its pieces so each can be studied.

definitions.meaning: read literally, to sense oneself unconstrained

explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to please themselves grants permission; read literally, the words mean sensing your own liberty.

clue.text: Bishop bathed in orange and gold light

indicators.note: bathed in means surrounded by, so the bishop's letter sits inside the colour

parts.note: flame is an orange-red colour
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A bishop is lit by an orange and gold glow.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, a source of illumination.

indicators.note: sound of tells the solver the answer is said the same as the canal's name

parts.note: the Kiel Canal crosses northern Germany

explanation.surface: The noise made by a narrowboat on the waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: A keel is also a flat-bottomed barge, once used on the river Tyne.
explanation.definitionFit: A keel or keelboat is a low flat-bottomed freight vessel.

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: A fuss is made about someone being promoted, as with song and dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' looks like the idiom for a fuss but splits into the definition and a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative poem set to music, so it is a kind of tune with words.

parts.note: St is an abbreviation for street, a way
roll means move steadily forward

explanation.surface: A way of moving forward is simply on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely saunter.

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Phoning a man's number over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call but is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something frequently means doing it repeatedly.

indicators.note: returned means the word for a girl comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a maid is a girl; the 's stands for 'is'
ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: A girl comes back earlier, covered in sparkly trimmings.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamanté is fabric trim studded with sparkling fake gems.

clue.text: The northern island builds gas unit

parts.note: t' is a northern English dialect form of the
Herm is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A northern island builds a gasworks.
explanation.walkthrough: In northern English speech 'the' is clipped to t'. Herm is a small island near Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, used in billing for supplied natural fuel.

clue.text: Order due to be given about first of August

indicators.note: about means going round, so the proper word surrounds the month's initial

parts.note: fit means proper or due

indicators.note: first of picks just the opening letter of the month

explanation.surface: An instruction says something must be done around the start of August.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative decree or command.

indicators.note: concealing means hiding, so the money letter sits inside the rearranged soldier
possibly signals the soldier's letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, the British money unit

explanation.surface: A guardsman is secretly hiding cash, which makes him a bad lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges GRENADIER; 'concealing' puts L (from the Latin libra, pound) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringleader heads a group causing mischief or revolt.

clue.text: Monarch beset by difficulty shows spite

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the monarch's name is placed inside the trouble

parts.note: a mess is a difficulty
Anne was Queen of Great Britain 1702-1714

explanation.surface: A queen in trouble lashes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanness can be nastiness or unkindness, much like malice.

clue.text: Spot one with note and go inside

parts.note: a dot is a spot
I is the Roman numeral for one
me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singer spots someone, hits a note and heads indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go inside' is slang for going to prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve a prison sentence is to be locked up, slang for going into jail.
